encoding.decision: Parity with Hermes (2026-10-13): TextEncoder, atob and btoa present and tested; TextDecoder absent, with a negative fixture, as on RN iOS and Android.

encode/no-argument.why: encode() has no default for its argument: a missing one is converted to the text "undefined", where the encoding standard's default is the empty string.

encode/undefined.why: encode(undefined) is converted to the text "undefined" for the same reason.

btoa/no-argument.why: btoa() converts a missing argument to the text "undefined" and encodes it, where Node throws a TypeError (ERR_MISSING_ARGS).

atob/no-argument.why: atob() converts a missing argument to the text "undefined", whose nine characters are not a valid base64 length: an Error, where Node throws a TypeError.

oracle.independence: Written from RN, Node and the pinned Hermes, not from the probe: RN's Libraries/Blob/URL.js, Libraries/Blob/URLSearchParams.js and the two files of src/private/webapis/dom/abort-api are bundled with nothing of the SDK's (no platform plugin, so none of its overlays) and run in a V8 context with the same cases the fixture runs in Hermes; the members of the four classes are read from RN's source with the TypeScript parser; Node's own TextEncoder, atob and btoa answer the encoding cases, Buffer checks the UTF-8 bytes, and a table of fourteen documented deviations says where Hermes answers otherwise and is required to differ from Node; the hermesvm binaries are scanned; every verdict of the probe is derived again from the report's raw observations.

expectationFile.note: The file the probe judges against. The runner requires it to equal what the oracle derives, so a change in RN, Node or the Hermes pin that moves an answer fails there.

limits: The fetch and XMLHttpRequest integration is the signal's: that an abort reaches the request and ends it as RN's code says. The transport, redirects, TLS and bodies are the networking suite's.

RN's XMLHttpRequest takes no signal option; the XMLHttpRequest case wires the signal's abort event to xhr.abort(), the way an application does. fetch is the one RN API that reads a signal (whatwg-fetch, version in environment.whatwgFetch).

URLSearchParams.sort orders keys with localeCompare, which is the engine's: the cases use ASCII keys, and the order is the one ICU gives V8 and the Apple Hermes gives, in the default locale. Another locale could order them otherwise.

Android's libhermes is not part of this repository's pins; the claim that its Hermes has no TextDecoder rests on the decision and on the iOS, tvOS and visionOS slices of the same release, which the oracle scans.
The headless desktop host only; no mobile export has run this bundle.
